subject: Shoreline rebaseline — MAP update and credit trigger request
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@shorelinehealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@shorelinehealth.com>, procurement@shorelinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoints and go-live window

Hey Laura,

Quick update from our side — the clinical validation window slipped by two weeks after the last infection-control audit. That pushes our acceptance window out and unfortunately impacts the go-live we had penciled for the end of June.

We need to understand the levers you can offer for preserving our commercial cadence. Specifically:
- Can Redwood accept a revised MAP that moves the final acceptance date by 14 days without re-pricing?
- Is there a short-term credit or bridge for milestone-linked invoices if we confirm a new timeline this week?

Tom and I can jump on a 30-min sync today if that helps. Procurement is watching timelines tightly.

Thanks,
Marta
Director, Clinical Ops
Shoreline Health

(Attachment: clinical-audit-summary.pdf)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@shorelinehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@shorelinehealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com> , Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 14:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoints and go-live window

Marta — thanks for the heads up and the audit summary. Sorry to hear about the delay; totally understandable.

At a high level: yes, we can keep the same commercial terms while rebaselining the MAP for a 14-day shift. There are two practical items we need to align on quickly:
1) A revised MAP PDF that lists the new acceptance milestones and updated sign-off owners (we'll version it v2).
2) A short credit term-sheet that defines a single milestone credit if the original invoice schedule is impacted by the delay. That gives you a cushion while preserving the total contract economics.

Proposed next steps:
- I'll circulate a draft MAP v2 and the credit-trigger term-sheet by EOD Friday.
- Karthik, can you confirm whether the Dedicated capacity hold we placed can be shifted without incurring penalty for a 14-day shift? If not, we should surface the delta so Marta's procurement team can weigh options.
- Grace, please prepare a quick acceptance checklist that maps to the clinical audit items so we can reduce ambiguity on sign-off.

If you prefer, we can do a 30-min call now (I have 15:00 or 16:00 ET). Otherwise we'll send drafts and aim for a 1-hour joint review Monday.

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: none)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:11:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoints and go-live window

Laura / Grace — quick internal note following Marta's ask.

We can hold the Dedicated capacity reservation for a 14-day shift without charging the customer an extra reservation fee provided they accept one of the following:
- Option A: Move the reservation window by 14 days (no charge).
- Option B: Keep the original reservation and provide a one-off credit equal to two days of baseline throughput cost if they need a hard cutover earlier than the new window.

Operational caveats: if the customer's total committed GPU-hours are reduced in the eventual contract amendment, we will need to re-evaluate kernel licensing line items (rare but possible). I recommend we offer Option A + a clearly-limited credit-trigger (one milestone token) to avoid procurement pushback.

Laura: drafting the two small PDFs now — MAP v2 (with explicit sign-off owners) and credit-trigger-term-sheet — will send in 30 mins.

Karthik
Head of Dedicated Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: none)

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@shorelinehealth.com>
Cc: Tom Brennan <tbrennan@shorelinehealth.com>, procurement@shorelinehealth.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 17:42:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP checkpoints and go-live window

Hi Marta — appreciate the quick sync this morning. Per our call attached are:
- shoreline_rebaseline_MAP_v2.pdf (MAP v2: acceptance milestones moved by 14 days; sign-off roster; updated test owners)
- credit-trigger-term-sheet.pdf (one-time milestone credit if an invoice falls outside the new MAP schedule)

Summary of agreed items (TL;DR):
- Redwood will rebaseline the MAP by +14 days and keep the current pricing schedule intact.
- Dedicated capacity reservation will be shifted by 14 days (Option A) with no reservation fee change.
- If Shoreline elects to keep an earlier cutover and that causes overlap costs, Redwood will apply the one-time credit outlined in the term-sheet.
- Grace will own the acceptance checklist and will be copied on the final sign-off emails during the validation window.

Please review the two attached PDFs and reply with an explicit approval line ("Shoreline approves MAP v2 and credit-trigger term-sheet") so our legal/procurement teams can mirror the change in the amendment. Procurement, please note the HubSpot deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/DL-2026-0789.

Next steps:
- Shoreline to confirm via reply by Tue 2026-06-16 18:00 ET.
- Once confirmed we will issue a one-page amendment that both legal teams sign; Redwood will mark MAP v2 as the active plan.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: shoreline_rebaseline_MAP_v2.pdf; credit-trigger-term-sheet.pdf)
